To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
E2 increases GnRH secretion through the modulation of the excitability of hypothalamic GnRH neurons.

17β‐oestradiol modulates GnRH neuronal excitability by altering the expression of ion channels, including potassium, calcium, and small conductance Ca‐activated K+ channel, which contribute to burst firing pattern in GnRH neurons.
E2 increases the firing rate and burst firing of GnRH neurone by increasing the expression of potassium (KATPs and A‐type) and calcium (T‐type and L‐type) channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterisation of the E2‐sensitive targets in GnRH neurone and their roles in the control of GnRH neuronal activity.
understanding the mechanisms by which E2 modulates the excitability of the GnRH neurones, and how these actions of E2 contribute to the cyclic activity pattern of GnRh neurones.
elucidating the molecular mechanisms by which E2 regulates the excitability of the GnRH neurones to understand the cellular and molecular basis for the cyclical Gn RH secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E2 increases GnRH neuronal activity through both presynaptically and postsynaptically mediated mechanisms.
E2 increases the activity of the KATP channels and reduces the activity of L‐type calcium channels in GnRH neurons, which leads to an overall increase in excitability and GnRH neuronal activity.
E2 regulates GnRH neuronal activity by modulating the excitability of both presynaptic terminals and GnRH neurones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

E2 is a critical regulator for GnRH neuronal activity through the regulation of multiple ion channels, and that this may be a critical step in the regulation of the GnRH neuronal activity during pro‐oestruss.

E2 increases the expression and activity of the hyperpolarising K+ channels, which decreases the firing frequency and burst activity of GnRH neurons, and increases the excitatory Ca2+ currents, which enhances the GnRH release.
E2 increases the activity of GnHRH neurones by increasing their excitability, which is achieved by modulating multiple ion channels in the GnRH neurones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
E2 is a potent modulator of GnRH neuronal activity, and that the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying this regulation are complex.
E2 has a significant effect on the expression and function of numerous ion channels that are important for regulating the excitability of the GnRH neuronal network.
